image_description: A close-up photograph of a butterfly resting on a light-colored, textured rock surface. The butterfly has its wings held vertically closed, displaying the ventral (under) side. The hindwing is predominantly greyish-brown with a distinct row of dark ocelli (eyespots) bordered by lighter rings. The forewing shows a patch of orange near the apex with a single large black eyespot. The body is fuzzy and brown, and one clubbed antenna is clearly visible against the background.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The right antenna is clearly visible, extending upwards with a distinct thickening at the tip (club), characteristic of butterflies.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Satyrid butterfly with moderately sized wingspan.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall morphology, wing shape, and resting posture are consistent with the Satyrinae subfamily (browns/ringlets).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings uniformly brown to dark brown with small eyespots (ocelli) arranged in rows.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral hindwing displays a clear submarginal row of ocelli. While the base color is greyish-brown rather than uniform dark brown, this matches the cryptic ventral patterning described in the taxonomy for this species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings held closed at rest revealing cryptic ventral patterning.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The butterfly is photographed in profile with wings pressed together, showing the underside pattern which serves as camouflage against the rock.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brown body integument matching wing coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The thorax and abdomen are covered in brown hairs that blend well with the darker tones of the wings.
High-resolution detail shows significant hairiness (setae) on the thorax and head.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While ringlets are Nymphalids and possess reduced forelegs, they are tucked against the head and are not resolvable in this specific angle/lighting. Marking untestable to avoid false negative.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (three tagmata).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The division between head, thorax, and abdomen is visually apparent, consistent with insect anatomy.
